A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, estimators, central contributions, and experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 Appendix C reports original synthetic autoregressive-system experiments, including estimation-error results for full-rank, low-rank, and misspecified-context settings in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results in Appendix E, Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: The constrained least-squares estimators, per-lag rank constraints, context truncation, and group-nuclear-norm relaxation are retained. The new approximate-minimizer analysis extends guarantees without introducing a different optimization algorithm or implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic autoregressive identification tasks: full-rank estimation, low-rank estimation, and shortened-context estimation. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain OLS and group-nuclear-norm-regularized estimators. Figure 4 retains the same regularized comparisons against unregularized OLS; cited theoretical methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The matrix-generation procedure, dimension/context/trajectory sweeps, sequence-length schedule, estimation-error metrics, and hyperparameter searches are unchanged between v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix E. The approximate-minimizer extension introduces no new experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The parameter-scaling checks, context-misspecification comparisons, and low-rank regularization analysis in Figures 2–4 are retained. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three independent seeds and omit variance displays because the curves overlap and variance is described as small. No empirical uncertainty-reporting practice changes; revisions to theoretical probability bounds are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 retain identical plot content and the same findings, including overlapping misspecification curves and lower low-data estimation errors with low-rank regularization. No empirical result entries are added, removed, or updated.

T1.justification: v2 substantially revises the concentration and discretization arguments, including the Freedman-based lemma, noise-supremum bounds, and an explicit blockwise low-rank covering argument. The main confidence dependence changes from v1's O(log(1/delta)) claim to cubic logarithmic dependence in Appendix C.5, with revised logarithmic factors and OLS sample-size conditions. New Appendix D derives guarantees for approximate empirical minimizers.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three central contributions: near-i.i.d. rates without mixing-time penalties, improved dimensional dependence under low rank, and statistical benefits from shortened contexts in stable systems. The revised technical guarantees preserve these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds practical interpretations connecting the rates to training-loss thresholds and tolerable optimization error. Remark C.3 explains the sources of the logarithmic factors and discusses possible reductions using bounded noise or chaining. The limitation concerning misspecification in marginally stable systems was already present in v1.

D1.justification: The disclosed Python, PyTorch, and NumPy usage, matrix initialization, rank construction, and learning-rate and regularization grids are retained. No new implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is provided.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to first-order system identification remain the same. Changes such as Tu et al. (2023 to 2024) update publication metadata. Candès and Plan (2011), used in the expanded covering argument, was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main narrative is retained with widespread copyediting and a reordered mixing discussion. The proof sketch moves from Section 6 to Appendix A, appendix headings and proof exposition are reorganized, and publication and funding text is updated.

P2.justification: The four figures retain their plots, axes, and legends, but surrounding text and placement are adjusted. Figure 2's reference-line caption changes from sqrt(gamma/beta) to gamma/beta and gamma/bar(beta). Conference headers and equation formatting also change.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the central theoretical account by revising the martingale and covering arguments and replacing v1's linear-log confidence claim with explicitly derived cubic-log dependence. Appendix D also addresses the restriction to exact empirical minimization through an optimization-error analysis. These changes improve the precision, completeness, and applicability of the theoretical guarantees. The more conservative logarithmic factors are a material qualification, while the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
